core_idea: A function increases where its derivative is positive and decreases where its derivative is negative.
what_students_need_to_understand: This is a core link between derivative sign and function behavior used across graph and FRQ reasoning.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by testing derivative sign on intervals and translating that sign into increasing or decreasing behavior.

title: Using the First Derivative Test
core_idea: The first derivative test classifies local extrema by how f' changes sign around a critical point.
what_students_need_to_understand: It is a point-rich justification pattern because the conclusion depends on evidence on both sides.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by showing f' changes from positive to negative for a local maximum or negative to positive for a local minimum.
answer_move: Check f' on the left and right of the critical point before naming the extremum.

weak_answer: I would write the final value or conclusion without showing why it follows.
point_attaining_answer: Check f' on the left and right of the critical point before naming the extremum. Then make the scoring connection explicit: You earn points by showing f' changes from positive to negative for a local maximum or negative to positive for a local minimum.
common_point_loss: Saying f'(c)=0 is enough to prove a maximum or minimum.

core_idea: The candidates test compares function values at endpoints and critical points to identify absolute extrema on a closed interval.

how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by identifying all candidates, evaluating the original function at each one, and selecting the largest or smallest value.

title: Determining Concavity
core_idea: Concavity describes whether slopes are increasing or decreasing and is determined by the sign of the second derivative.
what_students_need_to_understand: It connects derivative behavior to graph shape and prepares students for inflection and second-derivative reasoning.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by finding where f'' is positive or negative and translating that sign into concave up or concave down intervals.
answer_move: Make a sign chart for f'' and state concavity on intervals.

common_point_loss: Using f' sign to decide concavity instead of f'' sign.

title: Using the Second Derivative Test
core_idea: The second derivative test can classify certain critical points using the sign of f'' at the point.
what_students_need_to_understand: It is efficient when it applies, but students must know its limits when f'' is zero or undefined.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by confirming f'(c)=0 or undefined as needed and then using f''(c) to classify the local behavior when possible.
answer_move: Check the critical point first, then use f''(c)>0 for local minimum or f''(c)<0 for local maximum.
mini_example_question: A calculus prompt asks you to justify a conclusion involving Using the Second Derivative Test. What should your work and sentence make clear?
weak_answer: I would write the final value or conclusion without showing why it follows.
point_attaining_answer: Check the critical point first, then use f''(c)>0 for local minimum or f''(c)<0 for local maximum. Then make the scoring connection explicit: You earn points by confirming f'(c)=0 or undefined as needed and then using f''(c) to classify the local behavior when possible.
common_point_loss: Using the test when f''(c)=0 and treating an inconclusive result as a conclusion.
